gauntlet: question
I've recorded your approach choice: reuse the existing CSV serializer and paging, with the button beside the report title. Before the design rounds, I need a decision on the ticket's third row, because I can't drop a ticket row without your explicit call:

`- [ ] The export of a 10k-row report completes in under 60s.`

How should the spec treat this row?

A) in-scope - a 10k-row report exported through the reused serializer and paging finishes in under 60s, proven by a timed test on a 10k-row fixture
B) deviates: the timing guarantee isn't needed this sprint; the export ships without a stated time bound
C) deferred: a follow-up ticket that owns the 10k-row timing (name the ref, e.g. `acme/widgets#NN`)
D) repair the ticket - /skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77 row 3 "The export of a 10k-row report completes in under 60s." - the reporter considers it beyond this sprint's need

Recommendation: A - The approach you chose already pages through rows, so the 60s bound is a check on that path rather than new work. One timed 10k-row test keeps the ticket's contract whole in this gauntlet. If the row truly doesn't belong on the ticket, choose D so the ticket records that, rather than having only the spec disclose the gap.

gauntlet: question
The button will sit beside the report title, using the existing CSV serializer and paging. Dropping the timing requirement changes an explicit acceptance criterion in acme/widgets#77:

- [ ] The export of a 10k-row report completes in under 60s.

How should we handle that row?
A) in-scope - retain the 10k-row, under-60s requirement and verify the chosen implementation against it.
B) deviates: this sprint excludes the 10k-row, under-60s performance requirement - ship the export without that guarantee.
C) deferred: a follow-up ticket or spec path you provide - move the performance requirement out of this sprint.
D) repair the ticket - /skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77 to revise this row because you have identified it as beyond this sprint’s needs.
Recommendation: D - align the ticket’s explicit contract with your intended sprint scope before approving the design.
